answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource, such as a hardware-attested key or a refundable deposit, before it can trade. Reputation then accrues slowly through attested work, like a reef built coral by coral, so fake identities cannot buy trust overnight. Peers mirror each other's attestations, cross-checking histories so one compromised account cannot vouch for an army of clones. When a gale of new accounts appears, rate limits and stake slashing raise the cost of flooding the network, making large-scale fakery uneconomic.
